subject: internet blackout
title: What If a Country Switched Off Its Internet? Egypt Did, for 5 Days

scenes.text: What if a government switched off the whole internet? Egypt did it in 2011.
Just after midnight on January 28, 2011, during mass protests, Egypt's main providers stopped routing traffic. Within minutes, the link to the outside world fell to a trickle.
About 80 million people, offline. Banks, airlines, call centres and online businesses froze.
The OECD put the cost at about 18 million dollars a day, 90 million over five days, in a country where telecoms were 3 to 4 percent of the economy.
The protests carried on anyway, in the streets. On February 2, the switch was flipped back on.
Governments kept doing it. In one year to mid-2016, 81 shutdowns in 19 countries cost at least 2.4 billion dollars.

description:
What if a country cut itself off from the internet? Just after midnight on 28 January 2011, during mass protests, Egypt's major internet providers stopped routing traffic and the country of about 80 million went dark online for five days, until 2 February.
The OECD estimated the direct cost at about 18 million dollars a day, at least 90 million in total, in an economy where telecoms and internet services made up 3 to 4 percent of GDP. A Brookings study later counted 81 shutdowns in 19 countries between July 2015 and June 2016, costing at least 2.4 billion dollars.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: WHAT IF THE INTERNET WENT OFF?
first_comment: The OECD's 90 million figure only counts direct losses; the long-term hit to investment was never measured. How long could you go without the internet, and what should we run through next?
